comments.content: `map[err]` reads through the prototype chain, so an untranslated message that happens to equal an inherited key (`constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `__proto__`, …) returns an inherited function instead of a string. That breaks the documented `string` return and propagates a non-string into `showTemporaryNotice({ type:'error', text })` / `new Error(...)` in the callers. The same file already guards the identical code→value lookup pattern with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(map, id)` (line 173); apply the same guard here.

Comment 1: friendlyForkError prototype chain.

Content: `map[err]` reads through the prototype chain; a message like `constructor`/`toString`/`__proto__` returns an inherited value (a function) instead of a string, breaking the documented `string` return and, in AppTab, pushing a non-string into `showTemporaryNotice({ text })`. The same file already uses `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(map, id)` (line 173) for the identical lookup pattern. Suggest guarding with hasOwnProperty.

suggestion_code:
```js
  if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(map, err)) return map[err]
  return /^[a-z0-9_-]+$/i.test(err) ? fallback : err
```
Hmm, the existing_code is the single return line. I'll provide suggestion replacing that one line:
```js
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(map, err) ? map[err] : (/^[a-z0-9_-]+$/i.test(err) ? fallback : err)
```
Note: nested ternary? No, it's a single ternary. Fine (nested ternary prohibition — this is one ternary). Actually the original already has a ternary. OK.

Comment 2: The pre-init POST result ignored. Should I include? Let me decide... I'll include it as low severity, framed around silent failure. Hmm. Let me think about whether a reviewer would consider this valid and non-noisy. The code comment claims "幂等保护" and the step is described as 关键修复 (critical fix), yet its failure is fully ignored — if the POST fails, the subsequent PUT reports `workspace-not-found` ("未找到工程画布，请重试") which doesn't point to the real cause, and the original bug resurfaces silently. I think it's a fair low/medium maintainability comment. I'll include it.

existing_code:
```
  if (!existingWs || existingWs.ok === false) {
    await doRequest('/omnimux-workflow/api/workspaces', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: { id: workspaceId, name: projectTitle },
    }).catch(() => null)
  }
```
suggestion:
```
  if (!existingWs || existingWs.ok === false) {
    const inited = await doRequest('/omnimux-workflow/api/workspaces', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: { id: workspaceId, name: projectTitle },
    }).catch(() => null)
    if (!inited || inited.ok === false) {
      const rawErr = inited?.body?.error || inited?.body?.message
      throw new Error(friendlyForkError(rawErr, '初始化工程画布失败'))
    }
  }
```
Hmm, careful — the tool matches the existing_code to insert the comment. I'll provide suggestion_code.

Hmm, but is this suggestion aligned with intent? The intent may be best-effort init so that the PUT still works if the workspace already exists (race). If we throw on POST failure, we'd fail the fork in cases where the workspace actually exists (e.g., GET failed transiently but POST also failed because it exists... but POST create overwrites, doesn't fail on existing). Actually POST create never fails for an existing id (it overwrites). So throwing on POST failure is safe. But it adds failure modes. Hmm, maybe a milder suggestion: check `ok` and surface/log. I'll keep the suggestion but soften the wording: "consider surfacing the init failure (or at least not discarding it)".

Actually, hmm — I realize there might be a subtlety: if the POST fails because the workspace already exists... no, create doesn't check existence. Fine.

Let me decide severity: low. Category: maintainability.

Should I include comment 2 at all? I'll include it — it's a legitimate observation about the newly added critical step. Keep it concise.

Let me now write the final response.

comments.content: The result of this "关键修复" init call is fully discarded: `.catch(() => null)` swallows a thrown/network error and the `ok === false` case is not inspected. If the seeding fails, execution continues to the PUT, which then reports the original `workspace-not-found` symptom ("未找到工程画布，请重试") — masking the real cause (e.g. `not-local` 403, `invalid-id`) and silently re-introducing the bug this block is meant to fix. Consider checking the response and surfacing the failure with `friendlyForkError` instead of ignoring it.
